title: Index-lifecycle fixture oracle, v0
description: Ground truth for one entity observed at a fresh index and then followed through mutations of the indexed world. Package 1's oracle-v0 asks what a graph knows; this asks what happens to what it already said. The four per-state questions are kept separate on purpose: a fast reindex answers only the first of them.

entity.description: The single symbol followed across every state.

observation.description: The fact handed to the consumer at the fresh state. Every later state is scored against THIS, not against a re-query -- the point of the package is what happens to evidence already in a consumer's hands.

mutation.description: Command that produces this state from the committed baseline. Null for the fresh state. States are absolute, not incremental.

graph_current.description: What a FRESH query should return once the index has converged on this state. Omit when the entity no longer exists.

questions.description: The four properties scored per state. They are recorded separately because a system can satisfy any one of them while failing the others, and because passing the first is routinely mistaken for passing the rest.

graph_current_correct.description: Q1 graph freshness. Should a fresh query at this state return the correct answer? Effectively always true once converged; recorded so that failing it is distinguishable from failing the rest.

stale_signal_required.description: Q2 staleness signaling. Must the consumer that took the observation be told it no longer holds? A rebuilt index that emits nothing fails here while passing Q1.

old_observation_valid.description: Q3 invalidation. Does the fact handed out at the fresh state still hold in this world?

action_admissible.description: Q4 post-invalidation admissibility, and the alarm. May an action derived from the OLD observation still be presented as safe to take? Where this is false and a system says otherwise, the result is a false-safe of the most dangerous kind: the tool is not wrong about the world, it is wrong about what it told you earlier.
